bullets: tizujccrTvE game 4 (video 676.8-900.9s), win over an Electro Giant beatdown deck (Phoenix, Bowler, Tombstone, Evolution Archers, Barbarian Barrel, Tornado, Lightning). Ryley calls his own list "this type of log bait deck" at t=757.

The game is decided at clock 1:50-1:39 by a Wall Breakers + Goblin Barrel double at t=738.7/739.7 after the opponent spends Barbarian Barrel on the Magic Archer: enemy towers go 4400/4527 to 2304/1907 in about four seconds — "this guy just got completely cooked already."

The stated core loop is a two-stage bait: Goblin Barrel first to draw Barbarian Barrel, then Wall Breakers plus a bridge Magic Archer behind it (t=791-796), repeated at t=789-806 and again in overtime at t=882-889.

Defence is entirely cheap and reactive: Tesla placed to deny Lightning value ("we do it up top just to make sure that he can't get any lightning value", t=735), Skeletons and Fire Spirit for 1 elixir each as kites, Royal Delivery on clumped pushes, and Ronin only when far ahead on elixir.

Ryley's stated reason the deck works: "the one elixir cards are just too strong, man. We get too many good trades out of them" (t=788), and the matchup verdict "early E-Giants against this type of log bait deck is just like a death wish" (t=755).

The Magic Archer is the Hero variant — he talks repeatedly about being able to "step back" with it (t=725, t=776), which is the Triple Threat teleport-and-decoy, and two own 2-elixir drops with no hand change at t=824.0 and t=828.0 line up with ability activations.

new_deck.rationale: Two cheap bait win conditions (Goblin Barrel and Wall Breakers) played to force small spells out, with a 2.9-elixir average cycle behind them; Ryley himself calls it a log bait deck.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: Both win conditions cost 3 and 2 elixir and answer to the same small spells, so the opponent can only cover one at a time — Ryley throws the Goblin Barrel first specifically to pull Barbarian Barrel, then sends Wall Breakers plus a bridge Magic Archer into the empty rotation. The Hero Magic Archer supplies the ranged pressure and the safety valve, since Triple Threat lets it retreat from splash instead of dying to it. Defence is three 1-2 elixir cards (Skeletons, Fire Spirit, Wall Breakers as a kite) plus Tesla and Royal Delivery, which is why the deck can stall a beatdown push and still be up elixir for the next barrel — "the one elixir cards are just too strong, man. We get too many good trades out of them." Ronin is the only expensive card and is held for moments when he is already ahead. The hard matchup rule Ryley states is that slow beatdown win conditions lose to it outright: "early E-Giants against this type of log bait deck is just like a death wish."
